text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- Austrian employers and unions will decide on flexible work hours, bowing to pressure by the government. An equally represented arbitration board is to be set up with experts presiding.
- Austria's Post and haulage companies are to join forces in parcel sevices to protect themselves against competition.
- Interior Minister Karl Schloegl's plans for a more restrictive immigration policy has been criticised by both leftist and rightist parties as too harsh or soft respectively.
- Austria's trade balance deficit rose in 1996 to 93 billion from 88 billion last year. Exports to Asian markets have grown.
- Social Affairs Minister Lore Hostasch does not expect any further cuts in Austria's health system.
- Low orders at motor engineer Steyr Daimler Puch Antriebstechnik are expected to cost 135 jobs.
- Papermaker Nettingsdorfer's dividend will remain the same even though profits were halved in 1996.
- Cartonmaker Mayr-Melnhof will pay a 17-schilling dividend for 1996 after none in 1995 as pre-tax profits were up 63 percent.
- Austria celebrates its third bronze medal by Andreas Schifferer in the Giant Slalom at the Skiing World Championships in Italy.
DIE PRESSE

- Austria's only private mobile phone provider max.mobil has accused its competitor state-owned Mobilkom of using frequencies illegally. The Transport Ministry's telephone authority has denied the allegations as unfounded.
- A fund to subisdise research technology spent 1.79 billion schillings in 1996.
- Austria's Greiner and Belgium's Recticel have increased cooperation to become Europe's market leader in foam production.
KURIER
- The Chamber of Economy has delayed the liberalisation of Austria' trade regulations by publishing a statement on the issue, which requires further investigation.
- Due to high sales of Creditanstalt preferred shares in London the share ratings are falling. However the swapping of the shares by Bank Austria will still go ahead.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT

- An energy holding in Styria is ready to start this spring. Regional suppliers Steweag and Steg will be integrated in the new holding. Whether municipal supplier Grazer Stadtwerke will join the holding is still unknown.
